summary: Across 1,003 live (non-archive) .md files carrying an `evidence_tier` field — 89 leading with [A], 235 with [B] — I found 10 documents where the declared tier exceeds what the document's own content supports. The single most consequential is on the published surface: `12_PUBLIC_SITE/canon/the-reciprocal-public-edition/index.html:6726,6802` tells readers the ladder's top rung is "[A] established external fact" and says it "are defined in the front matter" — but the front matter it cites (`13_BOOKS/the_reciprocal/00_front_matter.md:94`) says [A] is "analytic or machine-checked — follows from stated premises, and says nothing about whether the premises describe anything real." The published gloss inverts its own cited source, widening [A] from "says nothing about the world" to "external fact about the world," in the same sentence that promises "no claim should silently climb tiers." Three findings are silent promotions of the kind the lens names: ROSETTA_MUSIC.md tiers its own mirror-symmetry claim [C] in front matter and [S] in the body table; ASCENT_D5 tiers `P_node=min(Φ̂₄,V₄)` at [S] while three owners tier it [I], in a file whose status line reads "source owners control every claim tier." Four more are receipt-type documents wearing [A]: an HTTP-200 verification, a set of verbatim web quotations, and a founder's spoken instruction in a live session are all declared analytic/machine-checked when the corpus's own ladder puts observation and attribution at [B]. Underneath all of it sits a definitional split: [S] means "follows necessarily from stated premises" in the honesty protocol and "a considered choice, not a discovery" in the book front matter — two incompatible standards, both live, which makes every [S] adjudication in the corpus ambiguous.
method: Read-only, working tree at /Users/Yves/Documents/01_EMERGENTISM (branch reported as `main` by `git branch --show-current`, despite the session header naming `contracts/contribution-layer-2026-08-06`). ALL searches used /usr/bin/grep, never the shell `grep` function (which wraps `ugrep --ignore-files` and honours .gitignore); no absence claim below rests on the wrapper. (1) Established the canonical ladder by reading `02_EPISTEMOLOGY/01_EVIDENCE_TIERS/THE_HONESTY_PROTOCOL_STANDALONE.md:38-52`. (2) Enumerated declarations: `/usr/bin/grep -rIl --include='*.md' -E '^evidence_tier:' . | /usr/bin/grep -v '^./90_ARCHIVE/'` → 1003 files; same with `-E '^evidence_tier: *"?\[A\]'` → 89; `\[B\]` → 235; against ./90_ARCHIVE → 401 (excluded from findings). (3) Dumped every live [A]- and [B]-leading declaration with `-rn` and line numbers, then read the full front matter + relevant body sections of ~14 candidates with `sed -n`. (4) Silent promotions: took the owner tier table at `02_EPISTEMOLOGY/01_EVIDENCE_TIERS/00_THE_HONEST_POSITION.md:79` and grepped each claim family (`P_node`, `Rosetta`, `D0–D6`) for conflicting tier markers corpus-wide. (5) Public surface: grepped `12_PUBLIC_SITE/` for tier badges, then re-verified every hit against non-`.vercel` source so no finding rests on build output. (6) Freshness: ran `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` on all seven cited .md paths (untracked files INCLUDED, per the untracked-census trap). Two are dirty — `56_THE_PRODUCT_FORM_OF_THE_BALANCE.md` and `ASCENT_D5_THE_GAME_2026_08_05.md`; I ran `git diff -U0` on both and confirmed the working-tree edits touch neither quoted line, so both quotes are identical at HEAD and on disk. All other cited paths are clean. Every quote below was copied from the file, not paraphrased.
what_i_did_not_check: I did NOT verify the mathematics of any [A] claim — I checked whether the KIND of evidence matches the tier, never whether a theorem is true. So the ~80 mathematical [A] declarations in 05_COSMOLOGY/03_FORMAL_SYSTEM and 03_METHODOLOGY/02_THE_PAPERS are unadjudicated on content; several ("[A] chart identities", "[A] inherited projective mathematics") are plausibly correct scoping but I did not confirm the identities hold. I did NOT open the Lean file `09_TOOLS/05_FORMAL_VERIFICATION/EmergentismCheck.lean` or re-run any machine check, so every "machine-checked at one remove" claim in `14_THE_DISTILLATION/01_WHAT_IS_PROVED.md` is unverified by me — note that file itself records the build was NOT re-run this pass and that a prior measurement was found stale, so its figures are subject to the measured-findings-decay rule and should be re-run before anyone repairs on them. I read front matter for all 89 live [A] files but full bodies for only ~14; the remaining ~75 could hide body-level promotions like the ROSETTA_MUSIC one, which was invisible from front matter alone. I did not audit 90_ARCHIVE (401 declarations, deliberately out of scope), non-.md formats other than the public-site HTML, `.agents/skills/` references cited as grounds by the L3 audits, `00_PMO/`, or the untracked directories in the status snapshot. I did not run the corpus's own `09_TOOLS/01_SCRIPTS/check_*.py` gates, so I cannot say whether any existing checker already catches these. Findings 3 and 8 turn on which [S] definition governs — if the owner rules that [S] means "selected", finding 3 weakens and finding 8 resolves it.

findings.issue: Two incompatible definitions of [S] are simultaneously live, and they differ in evidential force. The honesty protocol makes [S] a derivation ("follows necessarily"); the book front matter makes [S] a selection with no derivational force ("not a discovery"). Every [S] label in the corpus is therefore ambiguous between "this is forced given premises" and "this is a choice I own" — and a reader applying the protocol's reading to a doc written under the book's reading will read a selection as forced, which is the precise defect the tier lens targets. This is upstream of finding 3 and of any future [S] adjudication.

findings.issue: An ACTIVE DOCTRINE close-out declares [A] for a spoken instruction. summary: The premise is wrong in a way that matters: only **4** live documents are absent from CORPUS_INDEX.jsonl, not ~346. The "~1727 live .md" figure is a `find`-style count that fails to exclude *nested* 90_ARCHIVE directories (93 files), the 91_COMPATIBILITY mirror lane (206), and dot-directory tool state (42 — Lean `.lake`, pytest caches). Reproducing the builder's own walk rules (build_corpus_index.py:38-41) gives 1,385 in-scope documents against 1,381 index rows; 1,385 − 1,381 = 4, and zero index rows point at files that no longer exist. The 4 absent docs are all recent commits (two 04_AXIOLOGY drafts from 3960d9be 2026-08-12 22:57, two ROSETTA_STONE themes files from 298232d3 2026-08-13 12:37) — the index simply has not been rebuilt since, despite an mtime of 2026-08-13 13:27 that is a touch, not a build. The real coverage story is inside the indexed rows, and the largest single defect is a harvest failure, not an absence: **55 documents declare `rosetta.d_register: 4` with a `d_register_basis` justification, and the builder drops every one of them** because `ROSETTA_KEYS` (build_corpus_index.py:50-51) does not list `d_register`. So the index reports 42/1381 (3.0%) D-coverage and labels it "the gap this index exposes", while 97/1381 (7.0%) is actually declared — and 00_THE_CORPUS_SPINE.md:185-187 still asserts "Not one document in the corpus declares its dimensional register in frontmatter." Field-wise: canonical_phrase null on 544 rows (39.4%), title 464 (33.6%), status 410 (29.7%), d_register 1,339 (97.0%). I verified these nulls are true absences, not parser misses — 0 harvest failures for canonical_phrase and title, 1 for status.
method: Read-only throughout; no corpus file written, edited, or moved (one scratch list at /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/find_live.txt, outside the working root). Instruments: `/usr/bin/grep` (absolute path — NOT the shell `grep` function, which wraps `ugrep --ignore-files` and honours .gitignore), `/usr/bin/find`, `/usr/bin/sed`, `/usr/bin/python3` heredocs, and read-only git (`git log`, `git show`, `git ls-files`, `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all`). (1) Read 09_TOOLS/01_SCRIPTS/build_corpus_index.py in full to recover the index's actual scope contract (EXCLUDE_PARTS = {.git, 90_ARCHIVE, node_modules, __pycache__, vendor, 91_COMPATIBILITY} plus any dot-directory ancestor). (2) Re-implemented that walk with pathlib.rglob and set-differenced it against the 1,381 index paths in both directions. (3) Reconciled the 1,726-file `find` figure into 1,385 in-scope + 206 91_COMPATIBILITY + 93 nested-90_ARCHIVE + 42 dot-dir = 1,726 exactly. (4) Field census over all 1,381 rows by direct JSON read. (5) HARVEST-vs-ABSENCE test: for every row with a null title/canonical_phrase/status, re-parsed the file's own frontmatter block with regex to check whether the key was actually declared and dropped — this is what surfaced the d_register finding. (6) Extracted every `*.md` reference from 00_THE_KERNEL_INDEX.md, 00_META/00_SETTLED_CANON_REGISTRY.md and 00_META/00_EMERGENTISM_INTERNAL_COMPLETION_REGISTER.md, resolved them against index paths, and reported field gaps for that kernel/canon-adjacent set (37, 42 and 21 indexed docs respectively). (7) `git ls-files --error-unmatch` and `git log -1` on the 4 absent files to prove they are tracked and committed, and `git show HEAD:...CORPUS_INDEX.jsonl | wc -l` (1,348) to separate the committed index from the dirtier working-tree copy (1,381, +42/−9). summary: Three of the 14 currently-green checkers are SOUND-BUT-BLIND, and the worst is wired into both gate.sh and CI. check_generative_base.py leaves its three declared bounds (WORD_LEN=10, CW_DEPTH=12, GRID=25) unasserted: cutting them to 4/3/3 keeps exit 0 while the PASS line openly prints the reduced scope ("PASS (12 values from all words to length 4 ...)"). The 2026-08-06 receipt already named two of these and proposed a "<1 hr" P1 repair; a repair landed in the working tree on 2026-08-13 but pinned only the successor operation, not the bounds — so the hole is 7 days old and still open, and I add CW_DEPTH as a third unpinned bound. check_barred_claims is blind at 33.4% of insertion points (366/1097) because claim_policy.py:53 suppresses any match preceded within 180 characters by "not"/"never"/"retired"/"forbidden" — in this corpus's hedging prose that exemption is close to ambient. check_established still accepts paraphrased verification inflation ("machine-checked end to end", "confirmed by the compiler", "true for every word") because FORBIDDEN_INFLATIONS is a literal substring list. Notably the corpus's own harness grades check_established SOUND — because both its seeded faults were drawn from that same allowlist, it tests the gate in the gate's own vocabulary. Nothing else is CANNOT-FAIL: 19 of my 29 effective probes went red, and I found working RED probes for four gates the in-corpus harness had left UNDETERMINED. Separately, one test file is strictly DOES-NOT-RUN (test_contact_limited.py executes 0 tests because setUpClass raises) and four currently-red checkers are invoked by nothing.
method: Read-only against working tree at HEAD d684aa84 (8 lane checkers dirty vs HEAD; never assumed tree==HEAD). findings.issue: The barred-claim suppressor is a 180-character lookbehind over arbitrary preceding prose. Any barred assertion that happens to follow the word 'not', 'never', 'cannot', 'no current', 'retired', 'forbidden', 'overclaim' or 'inflation' within 180 chars is silently exempted. In a corpus whose register is saturated with hedging and retraction language this exemption is close to ambient, making check_barred_claims blind at roughly one insertion point in three.
